clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old male with polysubstance use and recent COVID-19 presented with generalized abdominal pain and nausea. Initial labs showed anemia (Hb 8.5 g/dL), acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.3 mg/dL), elevated lactate, and mild inflammation. An initial abdominal CT revealed large heterogeneous gastric masses. A subsequent CT on ICU day 2 clarified these masses as hematomas resulting from a ruptured 2 cm saccular aneurysm of the left gastric or splenic artery, with associated hemoperitoneum. This CT also identified fusiform dilation of other mesenteric vessels, including the superior mesenteric artery, which are characteristic findings of vasculitis. The splenic artery pseudoaneurysm was successfully embolized. Investigations ruled out tertiary syphilis (negative VDRL/RPR), hepatitis B/C (negative hepatitis panel), and ANCA-associated vasculitis (negative ANCA). Despite not meeting ACR criteria, a diagnosis of Polyarteritis Nodosa (PAN) was made based on the elevated creatinine, characteristic imaging findings, and overall clinical picture. The patient was treated with high-dose IV methylprednisolone and IV cyclophosphamide.
